parts:

                        additionalMetadataTags =
                            c( # "EXIF:CameraModelName",
                              "MakerNotes:SerialNumber",
                              "MakerNotes:UserLabel",
                              "MakerNotes:AmbientTemperature",
                              "MakerNotes:MoonPhase",
                              "MakerNotes:BatteryVoltage",
#                              "MakerNotes:TriggerMode",
                              "MakerNotes:Sequence",
                              "MakerNotes:EventNumber",
#                             "MakerNotes:MotionSensitivity",
#                              "MakerNotes:FirmwareVersion",
                              "EXIF:ExifImageHeight",
                               #  "EXIF:SceneCaptureType",
                              "XMP:Subject",
                              "IPTC:Keywords"))

Error: something went wrong. I looked through all those 1 folders 
and now your table is empty. Were date/time information unreadable? 
Could species tags not be extracted (if IDfrom = 'metadata')? 
Or did you exclude too many species?

When I look at the metadata using the app "exifPro" the data time metadata are missing.
When I use exiftool all the metadata are present and correct.

However, the firmware on my Reconyx is v old, 2010.

I am using 
This is camtrapR 2.1.0 (DEVELOPMENT)
I think I am using a recent version exiftool - see screen shot.
How do I ask exiftool for its version?
I downloaded and installed a new copy of exiftool today and from the terminal successfully extracted all the metadata.

So why is my combination of images/camtrapR/exiftool failing to read the metadata for this single station. Ah - perhaps the date time is in the wrong format in this old version of the firmware?


David

messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] recordTable() failed to extract metadata
parts:
Hi David,

I tested it and recordTable worked without problems after running fixDateTimeOriginal first.

Note however that I did not use the "~/Desktop" path notation, used an absolute path instead. Personally I prefer giving absolute paths, and often construct them with file.path(). That way I usually only need to change one line at the top of a script if paths change, as long as the other paths relative to the main path are constant. And the script won't rely on whatever the current working directory is.

Not sure about years old R code. Something beyond my control might have changed also during the many changes from R3.x to R4. I don't think I made any changes that would break how camtrapR handles paths.

For the record, these were Reconxy HC600 Covert cameras. This model does not store date/time correctly, and it needs to be corrected with fixDateTimeOriginal.
